gangway-bellows.context: Two carriage ends joined by a folded rubber tunnel. Used for passenger connections between train cars and for rolling stock topics.

coach-position-indicator.context: A strip of three carriage sections with a pointer above a platform line. Used for boarding displays that show where each coach stops.

car-stop-marker.context: A numbered board on a post at a platform edge beside two rails. Used for signs that mark where a carriage door should stop.

train-destination-display.context: A train front with a wide text sign above the windshield. Used for route displays, headsigns and destination information.

portable-ticket-printer.context: A handheld machine with a screen and keypad and a ticket coming out of the top. Used for conductors issuing fares on board.

refrigerator-car.context: An enclosed freight wagon with a snowflake on its side and a cooling unit at one end. Used for chilled and frozen goods by rail.

centerbeam-car.context: A flat freight wagon with a tall central spine and end walls holding stacks of lumber. Used for timber and building material shipping.

mail-car.context: A rail carriage with an envelope on its side and a wide sliding door. Used for postal trains and mail transport.

baggage-car.context: A windowless carriage with two wide sliding doors and a suitcase on its side. Used for luggage and parcels carried on passenger trains.

side-dump-car.context: A rail wagon with its box tilted sideways on a piston and rocks tumbling out. Used for ballast, spoil and track maintenance.

compartment-coach.context: An old rail carriage with a row of narrow doors along its side, each with a window. Used for heritage and vintage train topics.

diesel-multiple-unit.context: A two-car passenger train with a driving cab at each end and an exhaust stack on the roof. Used for regional and commuter diesel services.

railbus.context: A small single rail car with a bus-shaped body, big windows and two axles. Used for light rural and branch line services.

locomotive-tender.context: A small wagon heaped with coal above a water tank, coupled behind a steam engine. Used for steam era and heritage railway topics.

open-excursion-car.context: A rail carriage with a roof on posts, open sides and benches. Used for scenic, tourist and heritage line rides.

wagon-brake-wheel.context: A large spoked hand wheel on a vertical shaft at the end of a freight wagon. Used for handbrake and wagon securing topics.

trolley-pole.context: A pole rising from a tram roof with a small wheel at its tip touching an overhead wire. Used for electric tram and trolley power pickup.

train-ferry.context: A ship hull with a train carriage on rails shown inside it. Used for rail ferries that carry rolling stock across water.

railway-roundhouse.context: A top view of a semicircular engine shed with stalls fanning out from a central turntable. Used for locomotive depots.

coaling-tower.context: A tall tower on legs over a track with a chute tilted down and coal falling. Used for steam locomotive fuelling depots.

train-shed.context: A large arched glass roof with ribs fanning out over station platforms. Used for terminus stations and station architecture.

hump-yard.context: A track rising over a small hill with a wagon rolling down into fanning tracks. Used for marshalling and classification yards.

loading-gauge.context: A hoop-shaped frame over a track marking the largest load that may pass. Used for clearance and height limit topics.

transfer-table.context: A top view of a movable bridge section on rails that slides sideways between parallel tracks. Used for workshops and depots.

train-wash.context: A train front passing between two tall brushes with water drops. Used for depot washing plants and cleaning.

wye-junction.context: Three tracks joined in a triangle. Used for track layouts that turn trains around.

passing-loop.context: A single track that splits into two parallel tracks for a short length and then rejoins. Used where trains pass each other.

balloon-loop.context: A track ending in a large round loop. Used for turning trains or trams back without reversing.

railway-siding.context: A main track with a short branch that leads off it and ends at a buffer stop. Used for storage tracks and spurs.

railway-junction.context: One straight track with a second track curving away from it like a Y. Used for branch lines and diverging routes.

track-crossover.context: Two parallel tracks joined by a single diagonal track between them. Used for switching trains between tracks.

railway-cutting.context: A cross section of a track at the bottom of a V-shaped cut with sloping sides. Used for earthworks and route engineering topics.

railway-embankment.context: A cross section of a track on top of a tall flat-topped mound of earth. Used for earthworks and raised track topics.

mail-bag-catcher.context: A trackside post with an arm holding a mail sack ready for a passing train to snatch. Used for historic mail pickup topics.

train-horn.context: Three trumpet-shaped air horns of different lengths on a bracket. Used for warning sound and locomotive signalling.

locomotive-bell.context: A bell hanging in a U-shaped yoke with a pull rope. Used for locomotive warning and heritage railway topics.

train-tail-lamp.context: The rear of a carriage with a window and one round lamp at the bottom. Used for the last vehicle marker light.

end-of-train-device.context: A small box with a flashing light on top clamped to the end of a freight train. Used for rear marker and telemetry units.

train-cab.context: A driver's desk seen from behind with a curved windshield, a dial and a throttle lever. Used for driver and cab control topics.

dead-mans-handle.context: A throttle handle with a button on top that the driver must keep pressed. Used for driver vigilance and safety control topics.

wheelset.context: Two flanged wheels joined by an axle and resting on two short rails. Used for bogie and undercarriage topics.

train-buffers.context: A carriage end with two round spring buffers on either side of a coupling hook. Used for coupling and shock absorbing gear.

brake-hose-coupling.context: Two flexible air brake hoses hanging down with their metal heads locked together. Used for air brake connections between wagons.

hand-signal-flags.context: Two flags on short sticks crossed at the handles. Used for manual signalling by railway staff.

train-derailment.context: A carriage tilted off the track with its wheels above the rails. Used for accident, incident and safety reports.

track-worker.context: A figure in a hard hat and striped vest holding a spike maul. Used for track maintenance crews and rail work safety.

station-master.context: A figure in a peaked cap with a badge and buttoned jacket holding a pocket watch. Used for station staff and timetable topics.

train-guard.context: A figure in a cap with a whistle at the lips raising a small flag. Used for train departure and railway staff topics.

railway-porter.context: A figure in a cap pushing a two-wheeled barrow loaded with suitcases. Used for station luggage handling topics.

platform-mirror.context: A large round convex mirror on a tall post at the end of a platform. Used for guards and drivers checking the train side.

trainspotting.context: A train front above a notebook and a pair of binoculars. Used for train spotting hobby and enthusiast topics.

screw-coupling.context: A hook at each end of a short chain with a central turnbuckle and a weighted handle. Used for linking wagons with a buffer coupling.

hot-box-detector.context: A low trackside box aiming wavy heat lines at the axle box of a passing wheel. Used for overheated bearing detection.

shunting-pole.context: A long pole with a curved metal hook at its tip lifting a chain between two wagons. Used for yard coupling work.

wagon-weighbridge.context: A rail wagon on a short track section over a platform scale with a dial beside it. Used for weighing freight loads.

rotary-car-dumper.context: A large ring holding a wagon upside down with coal pouring out below. Used for bulk unloading at ports and power stations.

tank-locomotive.context: A small steam engine with flat water tanks along its boiler and a cab, with no tender. Used for shunting and branch line steam topics.
